title: Pod → cloud identity: AKS vs EKS vs GKE
summary: A pod's Kubernetes service account becomes a cloud identity without node-level credentials or stored keys. Each cloud links the KSA to a cloud principal in its own way.

dimensions.label: Cloud identity
values: Google service account (or the KSA principal directly)

dimensions.label: Pod opt-in
values: Node pool runs the GKE metadata server

dimensions.label: Newer variant
values: EKS Pod Identity (no OIDC provider; association via EKS API)

notes: In all three, the annotation is a hint and the cloud-side trust check is the actual security boundary. An annotation alone grants nothing.
Isolation is per Kubernetes service account. Sharing one KSA across workloads shares the cloud identity too.
